catalogue_requests.summary: Write A1 to A6 to TARGET_AXIS for the KRL PTP loop

notes:
Passed on the fake backend with no gate warning (G1 to G9 pass). The evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level, and nothing ran on a robot. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: the R2 hardware backend is refused until a human sets reviewed_by in driver.lock.json. The catalogue class cap.motion.joint_position.v1 is not bound because it fixes the input in radians while the clone carries the native KUKA axis values and states no unit; the package uses x-cap.akselov.joint_position.v1 and records the catalogue request above. The clone states no joint travel range or motor envelope, so the move input is Limit.operator_required and site-limits.example.json is only a narrow fake-backend example, not a statement about a robot. The independent stop is the KRL program's $STOPMESS interrupt that calls IR_STOPM (opcua-control/opcua_ptp_movement.src:9-10); KukaVarProxy exposes no stop variable, so the @estop method only writes the last read axis position to TARGET_AXIS and keeps the socket open, and the KRL loop uses that position only after the running PTP finishes. NOT COVERED: the motor temperature array ($MOT_TEMP) because the clone subtracts a script-supplied offset whose value is not in the clone; the RSI path under rsi/, the OPC UA server scripts and the Visual Components model files, which are not part of the KVP device interface. The fake has no motion over time or kinematics: a TARGET_AXIS write changes $AXIS_ACT at once, while a real PTP takes time and the controller's $AXIS_ACT lags. The upstream KUKA class is generic and reports no robot model, so the package cannot verify that the connected controller is a KR 16-2; the device name follows the clone's KUKA_KR16_2 object and its control server. native.py loads xml/KUKAVARPROXY_communication.py by path with importlib.util only at hardware time; no install is needed and the gate never imports it. The upstream error handler raises SystemExit on a network or parsing error; the driver converts that process-level exit into a failed receipt. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted; the reviewer changed no file of the package. The KUKAVARPROXY client has no stop variable, so the e-stop writes the axis position it reads to TARGET_AXIS, which holds the next target where the arm is but does not end a PTP motion already running; the independent stop is the controller's own $STOPMESS interrupt (estop_physical_ref), as for every KUKA KR C4. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required: the licence is not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published before it.
